decisions.reason: As a flagship product line close to the firm's core practice software and supported by its own R&D, it fits existing knowledge well and is likely to remain on the market.

The education institute extends the firm's training and practitioner-support capabilities, so despite being somewhat more service-oriented than software it still builds on related knowledge and is likely to be retained.

A remote support tool is adjacent to the firm's established support and software activities, making it understandable and useful within its existing capabilities, though it is less central than core modules.

Practice analytics closely complements the firm's installed software base and its direction toward digital, efficient practice management, so the firm has strong absorptive capacity to improve and commercialize it.
A complete dental practice bundle is very close to the firm's broad established offer and likely strengthens customer lock-in and cross-selling, which makes discontinuation unlikely.

A job and practice listing portal is relatively distant from the firm's core software and support knowledge base, so even with in-house R&D the firm is less able to learn from and develop it than its core-adjacent products.
